evals.name: path-lookup-cursor-keybindings
evals.prompt: I'm on macOS and I switched from VS Code to Cursor last month. Where does Cursor actually store my keybindings.json on disk? I want to copy it to my work laptop. Tell me the absolute path and confirm whether Cursor uses a separate folder from VS Code or shares one.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/keybindings.json (or equivalent), explicitly states Cursor uses a separate parent folder from VS Code (Cursor vs Code), distinguishing it from VS Code's path.

evals.name: scope-debug-machine-setting
evals.prompt: Help me figure out why my workspace setting isn't taking effect. In .vscode/settings.json I have `"telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off"`, but when I open the Settings UI it shows the value as "all" with no override indicator. The same setting works fine when I put it in user settings. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Correctly diagnoses that telemetry.telemetryLevel is application-scoped (or machine-scoped) and therefore cannot be overridden by workspace settings. Explains the setting-scope concept and points the user to put it in user settings (or notes it's already working there). Bonus for mentioning enterprise policy as a related cause.

evals.name: jsonc-validate-trailing-comma
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies that the file is valid JSONC (VS Code's format) but invalid strict JSON because of (a) the // comment and (b) trailing commas after `true`, after the closing `}` of the task, and after the closing `]`. Explains the JSON-vs-JSONC distinction and offers a fix (strip comments, remove trailing commas) for the CI pipeline. Bonus for suggesting the bundled vscode-jsonc-validate or a JSONC parser.

evals.name: cross-variant-migration-vscodium-to-cursor
evals.prompt: I'm migrating from VSCodium to Cursor on Linux. I have a working setup in VSCodium with custom settings, ~30 extensions, and a few keybindings. What's the most reliable way to transfer all of this? Specifically: do I just copy the User folder, or are there gotchas? Both are installed natively (not Flatpak/Snap).
evals.expected_output: Identifies the source path (~/.config/VSCodium/User/) and destination path (~/.config/Cursor/User/). Mentions the extensions dir is separate (~/.vscode-oss/extensions for VSCodium → ~/.cursor/extensions for Cursor) and not a simple copy. Warns about: extension marketplace differences (Open VSX vs Cursor's marketplace), settings sync as an alternative, and Cursor's own additional cursor.* settings. Bonus for mentioning .code-profile export/import as a portable bundle, or for warning that some extensions won't be available in Cursor's marketplace.
